svg.title: How the Purdue Hackers Jukebox works
svg.desc: An annotated sketch of the approved plan: silent attendee and organizer pages talk to a durable shared brain; an audio worker prepares files for the sole Firefox venue player. A timeline explains fifteen-minute master periods, one request, mix resumption, quotas, and the build order.
svg.text: PURDUE HACKERS / THE PLAN, ON ONE PAGE
Your picks join the night. One laptop makes the music.
A plan — not a live app yet.
Arrows carry requests, instructions or files. Only the venue player makes sound.
Scan the request QR on the wall.
Sign in with Purdue Hackers ID.
Saved position in a paused mix
You can jump to a spot in it.
Keeps a paused mix’s file safe.
A Spotify link is not audio:
match it to a playable recording.
Apple Music links need matching too.
Seek to a spot in the track
The ONLY place sound comes out.
Admin sees what the player ACTUALLY
did — not just what was asked.
No download, stream or hidden embed.
Only one display is allowed to play.
Master = the organizer’s music. Requests take one turn at a time.
Paused when a turn is due? Wait for the organizer to resume.
Empty turn = another full 15 minutes of master music.
With uninterrupted master music; a normal song still finishes first.
Prove it first, then connect the pieces.
Based on the approved plan • 30 Oct 2026 • Source support, server placement and real hardware still need proof.
